main_text.head: Epodus 2. versuum 14.
main_text.p: DEprehensa Euadne grauida ab Æpyto, consulitur oraculum Delphicum, interea parit Euadne in dume-to quodam.

Οὐδ' ἐλάθε.) Regis cura exprimitur in educanda casta puella: tamen præter votum eius corruptam deprehendit. κλέπποισι[?] Doricum pro κλέπτησι. Python vrbs à serpente Pythone ibi occisio ab Apolline: vel ὑπὸ τῆς Πυθοῦ τὰ μέλλοντα[?], quòd isthic de futuris oraculum homines consulerent. vnde & Apollo Pythius, & festa Pythia dicta sunt, & πυθάζειν responsa dare. Homerus, πυθοῖ ἐν ἀγαθῇ[?], & petricosam πετρηέσσαν[?] vocat, quòd ad Parnassum montem asperrimum posita sit. Celebre Apollinis adytum, quinque tantum lapidibus constructum esse aiunt, opus Agamedis & Trophonij: depraedatum fuit illud templum à Gallis Senonibus: qui postea cœlitus tempestate incredibili obruti fuerunt.
Ταῦτας Doricum ταύτης, & πάσας pro πάσοις etiam Doricè & ἀδὲ pro ἡδὲ. sic ζῶναν κατα-θηκα-μένα[?] pro ζώνη & κατα-θη-καμένη[?], & alia leuiora.

page.notes: Greek scholia are printed in italic type; several Greek words are doubtful at this scan resolution and are marked [?]. The Greek line "παρθένιοι παῖδες ... νομιζομένων παρθένων" is only partly legible. Printed spellings kept as they stand: "Pythia", "Trophonij", "Æpyto", "urbem". Long s printed as f in "refponfa" is read as "responsa". The last line "ceus" completes the word "Phoeni-ceus" and is the end of the text, not a catchword.
